title: Prime-localized transition base changes
statement: Let Λ be a preorder, A→B ring diagrams and D a diagram of B_i-modules. Let q_i be primes of B_i, contracting compatibly along every transition [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose A^l,B^l,D^l are diagrams with B^l_i-module structures, base-to-top maps φ_i, natural stage maps ρA_i,ρB_i commuting with the base-to-top maps, and numerator maps ζ_i commuting with module transitions. Suppose ρA_i presents A^l_i as localization at q_i contracted to A_i, ρB_i presents B^l_i as localization at q_i, and the B_i-linear maps induced by ζ_i (with action restricted through ρB_i) are IsLocalizedModule at q_i [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Suppose localized module transitions are semilinear. If the original canonical ring base changes B_i tensor over A_i A_j→B_j and module base changes B_j tensor over B_i D_i→D_j are isomorphisms with their pure-tensor formulas [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], then every localized ring transition map B^l_i tensor over A^l_i A^l_j→B^l_j presents B^l_j as a localization at a submonoid and takes b tensor a to B^l(f)(b)φ_j(a). Every localized module base change B^l_j tensor over B^l_i D^l_i is B^l_j-linearly equivalent to D^l_j, taking b tensor x to bD^l(f)(x). No colimit, finiteness, Noetherianity or local-hom hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Fix i≤j. Identify B_j with B_i tensor over A_i A_j using the given pure-tensor isomorphism. Invert q_i complements in B_i and the contracted q_j complements in A_j, giving the tensor of the localized factors over localized A_i. The commutative squares identify its product map to localized B_j. All inverted elements avoid q_j. Inverting the complement of the pulled-back prime then gives B_j at q_j by the localization universal property, so choose that complement as W.

Localize the original module tensor equivalence. Tensor-localization compatibility shows that extending the earlier localized module to localized B_j and localizing the original later module both localize B_j tensor over B_i D_i at q_j. The IsLocalizedModule universal property gives their unique linear equivalence. The original pure-tensor formula and ζ naturality prove the formula for numerator-one x, and invertible denominators extend it to all localized x.
